title: Resistors, capacitors, switches, batteries
blurb: Say what resistors, capacitors and inductors do, read switch types like SPDT, and know which batteries recharge.

T6A01.why: A **resistor** is the part that opposes current. Its job is to resist.
T6A01.trap: An inductor opposes *changes* in current, not current itself.

T6A02.why: A **potentiometer** is an adjustable resistor, so turning it changes volume.
T6A02.trap: A fixed resistor can't be adjusted.

T6A03.trap: Capacitance and inductance are set by capacitors and coils.

T6A04.why: A **capacitor** holds energy in the electric field between its plates.
T6A04.trap: An inductor uses a magnetic field instead.

T6A05.why: Conductive plates separated by an insulator describe a **capacitor**.
T6A05.trap: A potentiometer is a resistive track with a wiper, not plates.

T6A06.why: An **inductor** holds energy in a magnetic field around its coil.
T6A06.trap: Capacitors store energy in an electric field.

T6A07.why: A coil of wire is an **inductor**.

T6A08.why: SPDT = one pole, two throws: **one circuit is switched to either of two others**.
T6A08.trap: Switching two circuits at once takes two poles (DPDT).

T6A09.why: Component 3 has one blade and one contact: single-pole, single-throw, a simple on/off.
T6A09.trap: Double throw would show a second contact to swing to.

T6A10.why: NiMH, lithium-ion and lead-acid are all rechargeable, so **all of them** qualify.

T6A11.why: **Carbon-zinc** cells are single-use. The others listed can be recharged.
T6A11.trap: Nickel-cadmium, lead-acid and lithium-ion are all rechargeable.
